ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, ABCD is a square with a side length of \(a\). Point \(P\) is on the diagonal \(AC\), and line \(PB\) is drawn. Line \(PQ\) is perpendicular to \(BP\) and intersects segment \(CD\) at point \(Q\). When \(DQ = 2CQ\), what is the length of \(BP\)?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, draw PF$\perp$CD at point F, and PE$\perp$BC at point E.\\
Since square ABCD has a side length of $a$,\\
it follows that CP bisects $\angle$BCD, and $\angle$PEC=$\angle$ECF=90$^\circ$,\\
therefore PE=PF,\\
therefore quadrilateral PECF is a square,\\
hence EC=CF.\\
Since $\angle$BPE+$\angle$EPQ=90$^\circ$ and $\angle$EPQ+$\angle$QPF=90$^\circ$,\\
it follows that $\angle$BPE=$\angle$QPF.\\
Since $\angle$BPE=$\angle$QPF and $\angle$PEB=$\angle$PFQ=90$^\circ$ and PE=PF,\\
it follows that $\triangle$PEB$\cong$$\triangle$PFQ,\\
therefore PB=PQ, and BE=QF.\\
Since DQ=2CQ and CD=$a$,\\
it follows that QD=$\frac{2}{3}a$ and CQ=$\frac{1}{3}a$.\\
Let BE=FQ=$m$, then CE=$a-m$, and CF=QC+FQ=$\frac{1}{3}a+m$,\\
thus $a-m=\frac{1}{3}a+m$,\\
therefore $m=\frac{1}{3}a$,\\
hence BE=$\frac{1}{3}a$ and PE=CF=$\frac{2}{3}a$,\\
therefore BP=$\sqrt{B{E}^{2}+P{E}^{2}}$=$\sqrt{(\frac{1}{3}a{)}^{2}+(\frac{2}{3}a{)}^{2}}$=$\boxed{\frac{\sqrt{5}}{3}a}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a square ABCD, A is at the upper left, B is at the lower left, C is at the lower right, D is at the upper right; diagonal AC connects from A to C, point P is located on AC; connect from B to P; from P draw a line segment PQ to point Q on the right side CD, and the problem statement explains that PQ is perpendicular to BP. Reasoning: According to the coordinate method, let B=(0,0), C=(a,0), D=(a,a), A=(0,a). Because P is on diagonal AC, let P=(x,a-x). From DQ=2CQ and CD=a, CQ=a/3 can be obtained, so Q=(a,a/3). The slope of line PB is (a-x)/x. The slope of line PQ is [a/3-(a-x)]/(a-x)=(x-2a/3)/(a-x). Since PQ⊥PB, the product of the two slopes is -1, namely [(a-x)/x]*[(x-2a/3)/(a-x)]=-1, simplifying gives (x-2a/3)/x=-1, so x=a/3. Therefore P=(a/3,2a/3). Thus BP=sqrt((a/3)^2+(2a/3)^2)=sqrt(5)a/3.
